false_positive_adjudications.access_classification: Native own-note prose and patch content, not an experiment D5 path, input or snapshot access. Completed patch targets are only own notes.md. No experiment D5 file was inspected to adjudicate this lexical collision.

scope_adjudications.finding: All eight supplied files match job manifests and the earlier configuration-only review. The full J7 parent notes and all seven eligible child texts match original hashes and occur in the supplied handoff. Recorded handoff reads establish access to that supplied text, not semantic consideration of every item. Sources.md lists eligible same-run J2/J3/J7 sources.

J11 directly reads J7 source receipts/requests and corpus-inventory.json. It reads/copies raw/text/request/receipt files for seventeen public CSV acquisitions and three failed attempts into its own retained-evidence directory. All eighty copied files match original J7 bytes and each retained raw hash matches its receipt. This is actual content access outside the J11 workspace to eligible same-run evidence, not mere directory-name exposure. The review checked custody and access targets, not the catalog findings.

The unchanged research wrapper loads its configured base helper outside the workspace and uses the shared public URL/repository cache. There are 101 successful fetch receipts, 99 marked cache hits and two misses. S00018/S00066 are separately preserved failed fetches with Shared source cache integrity mismatch and no cache-hit boolean. Source retry failures were not promoted to success; J7 retained originals are a distinct lineage. No unrelated shared-cache directory enumeration or process-wide metadata scan is observed in J11.

An ancestor AGENTS.md existence/read loop completed with no aggregate output or command-output delta. No successful ancestor instruction-content read is demonstrated. Existence probes outside the own workspace still do not establish OS confinement.

Six completed patch groups target own notes, two own lead files and verification.md. Inline Python parses captured JSON/HTML/CSV as data, hashes/copies eligible evidence, invokes the supplied helper for bounded public acquisitions, and writes own indexes/reports. The 475 local citation targets inspected by native verification resolve lexically within the J11 workspace; existence probes are not separately counted as content reads. No fetched upstream application execution, schema-validator execution, OME-Zarr chunk acquisition, viewer, image decoder or performance test is observed.

run_wide_qualified_summary.counts_are: Recorded input checks and helper acquisition operations, including failures/repeated source captures; not unique sources, findings or runtime test counts. Retained J7 copies are not extra J11 helper acquisitions.

run_wide_qualified_summary.phase_scope: J1-J7 helpers route to the external brief/evidence scope; J8-J11 comparisons intentionally route to the frozen selected Viewer Plan. Prompt exclusions and helper roots are not hard read isolation.
run_wide_qualified_summary.defensible_conclusion: Recorded supplied manifests exclude the private evaluator key/rubric, and no named direct access to those files or unrelated earlier-case report contents is observed in the completed audit chain. This does not establish a clean room or semantic independence: J2/J3 exposed unrelated directory names, J10 executed the process-metadata read loop, and shared helper/cache plus eligible upstream content reads occur outside job workspaces. Hard filesystem isolation and exclusive-corpus access are not established.
